title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction: This page finishes the Scholion (§79) to Euler's theorem on the divisors of p^2+3q^2 and of f^2+fg+g^2. Two results come from earlier in the paper. The first is that -1 is a quadratic residue (QR) modulo a prime p exactly when p = 4n+1. The second, from §§76-78, concerns -3. If p = 3n+1, the cubic residues and their differences give a representation of a multiple of p as p^2+3q^2, so -3 is a QR. If p = 3n-1, no number f^2+fg+g^2 (equivalently p^2+3q^2) is divisible by p, so -3 is a non-residue (NR). Euler then sorts primes p > 3 into the classes 12m+1, 5, 7 and 11 and combines the two facts. He also uses the earlier result that residues are closed under products and that NR times NR is a residue, so the character of +3 follows from those of -1 and -3. The four cases are: (I) p ≡ 1 (mod 12): -1 QR and -3 QR, so +3 QR. (II) p ≡ 5: -1 QR and -3 NR, so +3 NR; neither ±3 is a residue. (III) p ≡ 7: -1 NR and -3 QR, so +3 NR. (IV) p ≡ 11: -1 NR and -3 NR, so +3 = (-1)(-3) is a QR. In modern terms, (-3/p) = (p/3) and (3/p) = 1 exactly when p ≡ ±1 (mod 12). Euler closes by calling this an 'egregia proprietas' reached by the 'rather oblique' route through cubes, and says a more natural route is greatly desired. The next page begins the analogous study of fourth-power residues using a primitive root.

ideas.what: Quadratic character of -3 mod p determined by p mod 3, derived via cubic residues and the form ff+fg+gg / pp+3qq
ideas.modern_name: Supplementary case of quadratic reciprocity for -3: (-3/p) = (p/3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (stated earlier; proofs via p^2+3q^2 in his work on forms); Lagrange; full reciprocity Gauss 1796/1801
ideas.where_published: E449 (Opuscula analytica I, 1783); related material in Euler's papers on p^2+3q^2 (e.g. E272, unsure of exact number)

ideas.what: Combining the characters of -1 and -3 multiplicatively to get the character of +3 by p mod 12
ideas.modern_name: (3/p) = 1 iff p ≡ ±1 mod 12; multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol
ideas.where_published: E449; also implicit in E262 and other residue papers

ideas.what: Explicit call for a more natural, direct proof of the ±3 criterion
ideas.modern_name: Direct proofs of supplementary laws (later answered by Gauss's Disquisitiones and Gauss-sum arguments)

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and well known. Euler's derivation of the ±3 criterion from cubic residues in E449 is documented in histories of reciprocity (e.g. Lemmermeyer, Weil). His wish for a 'more natural' proof was fulfilled by Gauss and is not an orphaned thread.
transcription_corrections: Long s forms throughout ('reſiduum', 'diuiſor') are rendered as 's' in this page's transcription, while the neighbouring pages keep 'ſ'; the readings are otherwise consistent with the image.
Case I: the image reads 'Hoc ergo in ordine residuorum occurrent +3 et -3', which the transcription matches; 'Hoc' agrees with 'Hoc' in the scan.
